title: Agentic Payment Protocol (v0.2) — specification
quote: AP2 considers five roles: Shopping Agent (SA), Credential Provider (CP), Merchant (M), Merchant Payment Processor (MPP), Trusted Surface (TS). The Checkout Mandate is provided by the Shopping Agent and verified by the Merchant. The Payment Mandate is bound to a particular Checkout using the cryptographic hash of the Checkout JWT. To prevent rainbow table attacks, the Checkout JWT MUST be signed using a digital signature scheme (e.g., ECDSA) and not a deterministic signature (e.g., Ed25519). Each AP2 Mandate type identifies its schema using the vct claim (e.g. mandate.payment.1, mandate.checkout.open.1).

title: google-agentic-commerce/AP2 — Reference repository
quote: Repository structure: docs/ (specification, flows, FAQ), code/sdk/python/ap2/ (Python SDK), code/samples/ (Python/Go/Android scenarios for human-present and human-not-present cards and x402), code/web-client/ (Vite+React demo). Apache-2.0 license. Spec site: ap2-protocol.org.

title: Announcing Agent Payments Protocol (AP2)
quote: AP2 was developed by Google with 60+ leading payments and technology companies (Mastercard, American Express, JCB, UnionPay, PayPal, Adyen, Worldpay, Salesforce, ServiceNow, Coinbase, MetaMask, Mysten Labs, ...). Three Mandate types — Intent, Cart, Payment — create a tamper-proof audit trail signed as Verifiable Credentials. Supports cards, real-time bank transfers, stablecoins, and the A2A x402 extension for crypto. Launched 2025-09-17.

title: AP2 SDK v0.1 mandate models (Pydantic)
quote: class IntentMandate(BaseModel): user_cart_confirmation_required: bool, natural_language_description: str, merchants: list[str]|None, skus: list[str]|None, requires_refundability: bool|None, intent_expiry: str. class CartContents: id, user_cart_confirmation_required, payment_request (W3C PaymentRequest), cart_expiry, merchant_name. class CartMandate: contents, merchant_authorization (JWT). class PaymentMandate wraps PaymentMandateContents { payment_mandate_id, payment_details_id, payment_details_total, payment_response, merchant_agent, timestamp }.

title: AP2 v0.2 schemas — checkout_mandate.json + payment_mandate.json
quote: checkout_mandate.json required [vct, checkout_jwt, checkout_hash]; vct const 'mandate.checkout.1'; checkout_jwt is the base64url-encoded merchant-signed JWT of the Checkout payload; checkout_hash is the base64url-encoded hash of checkout_jwt (sd_alg or sha-256). payment_mandate.json required [vct, transaction_id, payee, payment_amount, payment_instrument]; vct const 'mandate.payment.1'; transaction_id is the base64url hash of the checkout_jwt linking the two mandates; risk_data is an open object of risk signals collected by the trusted surface.

title: AP2 Flow Examples — Human Present and Human Not Present
quote: Human Present: the User directly approves the closed Checkout and Payment Mandates. Human Not Present: the User approves OPEN Checkout and Payment Mandates while the Agent, acting autonomously, presents them along with Agent-signed CLOSED Checkout and Payment Mandates. A Human Not Present flow can be turned into Human Present by the Merchant (or Credential Provider) returning an unresolved_constraint error. The Trusted Surface uses user_sk to sign and create the Payment Mandate and Checkout Mandate; the checkout_jwt hash permanently links the Mandates; the agent_pk is included as a confirmation claim to sender-constrain Mandate usage.

title: AP2 Agent Authorization framework
quote: This document defines two models for Mandate Delegation: User Credential and Trusted Agent Provider. The User Credential approach makes use of an Issuer external to the Agent that the Verifier trusts to guarantee the Trusted Surface; the Trusted Agent Provider approach makes the provider of the Agent the party trusted by the Verifier.

title: AP2 sample — Human-Not-Present with x402 (crypto rail)
quote: Human-Not-Present transaction using payment methods compatible with x402. The flow is triggered by a mock price drop or item drop event from the merchant. Once the price drops to a level acceptable to the agent (based on user intent), the Shopping Agent autonomously completes the purchase using the pre-authorized credentials and mandates, without asking the user for real-time confirmation. The Merchant Agent advertises support for x402 through its agent card and CartMandate. Skips manual steps like OTP.

title: Google's AP2: A new protocol for AI agent payments
quote: AP2 introduces three signed Mandates (Intent, Cart, Payment) carried as W3C Verifiable Credentials, each Mandate signed by the user's wallet or the agent's key, passed between parties as a verifiable JSON object.

title: AP2 Protocol Explained: Google's Agentic Commerce Standard 2026
quote: AP2 is Google's open standard for letting AI agents transact on behalf of users; the central innovation is Verifiable Credentials (VCs) acting as tamper-proof, cryptographically signed Mandates.

title: Sixty Organizations Joined Google's AP2 Donation to FIDO
quote: Google released AP2 v0.2 on GitHub on April 28, 2026, alongside donating the protocol to the FIDO Alliance for community governance. v0.2 added Human Not Present payments and Verifiable Intent (a tamper-proof log of user-authorized agent actions, co-developed with Mastercard and also donated to FIDO).

title: Google Agent Payments Protocol (AP2): Technical Guide & Implementation
quote: Technical guide describing AP2's mandate flow at implementation level: Intent → Cart → Payment, with the Shopping Agent constructing the cart, the user approving via a Trusted Surface, and the Credential Provider issuing tokens.
